family.summary: The everyday school office in one place: admissions, student records, fees, attendance, exams, transport, library, communication and more.
family.problem: Office work is spread across registers, spreadsheets and separate tools, so staff re-enter the same details and answers come slowly.
family.benefit: Staff could work from one set of records, spend less time compiling reports, and answer parents and leaders faster.
ai: AI-assisted drafting for health notes and admission remarks
Staff can ask questions of school records in plain words

subs.name: Student
subs.summary: Keeps each student's record in order: enrolment, profile, documents, health notes, certificates and I-cards, by section, class and division.
subs.problem: Scattered registers make finding, updating and certifying student details slow and repetitive.
features: Search students by class, division, name or GR number
Add students with an automatic GR number
Update chosen details for a whole class
Print certificates and I-cards from templates
See which students have missing documents
technology: AI-assisted drafting for health and vaccination notes
subs.benefit: Finding, updating and certifying student records could become easier for office staff.

subs.name: Admission
subs.summary: Takes a family from first enquiry to confirmed admission: enquiries, follow-ups, registration with documents, and confirmation.
subs.problem: Enquiries, follow-up dates and registration papers in different places make it easy to lose track of a family.
features: Log enquiries and follow-ups for each family
Track registrations with document and fee status
Confirm admission and add the student record
Export confirmation lists to Excel, PDF or print
Draft enquiry remarks with AI assistance
subs.benefit: Following up enquiries and moving families through registration and confirmation could become easier for the admission team.

subs.name: Attendance
subs.summary: Daily class attendance: choose the class and date, mark present or absent, and save the register.
subs.problem: Taking, correcting and sharing daily attendance on paper is slow.
features: Pick class and date, then load the register
Mark present or absent, or mark all together
School calendar holidays and Sundays block marking
Saving again the same day updates earlier marks
Sends app notifications to families for same-day marking
technology: Rules and automation for holidays and alerts
subs.benefit: Taking attendance and keeping families informed could become easier for teachers.

subs.name: Users
subs.summary: The staff directory: add and edit employee accounts, give each an access profile, record teacher subjects and lectures.
subs.problem: Keeping staff accounts and the right access for each person up to date is slow when records are scattered.
features: Add and edit staff accounts with access profiles
Record teachers' subjects and total lectures
Search and sort the staff list
Deactivate accounts instead of deleting them
Only administrators can assign administrator profiles
technology: Role-based access to view, add, edit and delete
subs.benefit: Adding staff, setting their access and switching off leavers could become easier for administrators.

subs.name: Front Desk
subs.summary: A front-desk log of parent and other visitors: who came, whom they met, why, and when they left.
subs.problem: Paper visitor registers make it hard to see quickly who met whom, when and why.
features: Log each visitor with student and staff member met
Record in time, out time and visitor photo
Choose parent or other visitor type
Staff see only entries addressed to them
Search the log; export to CSV, Excel or print
technology: Role-based access: staff see their own visitors
subs.benefit: Reception could keep a searchable record of visits, and staff could find the visits meant for them.

subs.name: Visitor Management
subs.summary: A gate register for visitors: who came, whom they met, why, with ID card and photo, and when they left.
subs.problem: Gate visits written on paper are hard to search, and leaving times are often missed.
features: Record gate visits with ID card and photo
Log direct or prior-appointment visits
Check visitors out from today's list
Welcome and exit text messages, when switched on
Search and export today's visitor list
technology: Visitor text messages through the school's gateway
subs.benefit: Gate staff could record and close visits quickly, and hosts could be told when a visitor arrives.

subs.name: Timetable
subs.summary: Class teacher assignments, the weekly timetable grid, and substitute-teacher cover for absent staff.
subs.problem: Clashes between periods and sudden teacher absences take time to sort out by hand.
features: Assign one class teacher to each class
Build the weekly grid by subject, teacher and period
Stops a teacher being booked twice in a period
Shows each teacher's remaining lectures while planning
Lists only available teachers as substitutes
technology: Rules and automation for clash checks
subs.benefit: Planning periods and arranging substitute cover could become easier for the timetable coordinator.

subs.name: Exam
subs.summary: Marks entry, co-scholastic grades, result file uploads and holistic progress card activities for each class and term.
subs.problem: Entering, checking and approving marks across many classes and sheets takes a lot of time.
features: Enter marks by term, class, subject and exam
Grades fill in from the school's grade ranges
Approve co-scholastic grades per class and term
Upload a result file for each student
Record holistic progress card activities per student
subs.benefit: Entering and approving marks could become easier, and results could be prepared from checked entries.

subs.name: Fees
subs.summary: Collects school fees at the counter or online, issues receipts, handles cancellations and refunds, and prepares auto-debit files.
subs.problem: Tracking collections, cancellations, refunds and pending dues across classes and months takes time when each is kept separately.
features: Collect fees with fine, discount and printed receipt
Cancel receipts or record refunds with remarks
Print circulars for students with pending fees
Parents can pay online through a school link
Export and import bank auto-debit files
subs.benefit: Front-office staff could see dues, receipts and refunds in one place, and parents could pay without visiting the school.

subs.name: Petty Cash
subs.summary: Records small day-to-day school expenses against named heads, keeps the bill image, and reports spending by date and head.
subs.problem: Small cash expenses are hard to trace later when the bill, the head and the amount are kept in different places.
features: Record expenses with date, head and amount
Attach a photo of the bill
Maintain a list of expense heads
Report spending by date range and head
Show the total spent for any period
subs.benefit: Accounts staff could find any small expense, its bill and its head quickly instead of searching old registers.

subs.name: Inventory
subs.summary: Runs the school store from requisition to purchase order, receiving, allocation, return and defective-item records.
subs.problem: Without a clear trail, nobody can say who asked for an item, who approved it, what was ordered or where it went.
features: Raise requisitions and approve quantities
Record vendor quotations and generate purchase orders
Negotiate order rates, tax and payment terms
Receive items against a purchase order
Allocate, return and log defective items
technology: Approval steps on requisitions and orders
subs.benefit: Store and purchase staff could follow each request from approval to delivery and see what is received, issued or returned.

subs.name: Transport
subs.summary: Manages vehicles, drivers, routes, stops and distance-based rates, and places each student on a bus, stop and shift.
subs.problem: Matching students to buses and stops by hand makes it hard to see which vehicle is full and who rides where.
features: Keep vehicles with seats, driver and conductor
Define routes and stops with pickup and drop times
Set distance-based rate slabs
Map students in bulk with seat check
Van-wise lists and summaries with CSV export
subs.benefit: Transport staff could see how full each vehicle is, who rides on which route and stop, and update mappings quickly.

subs.name: Hostel
subs.summary: Sets up hostels, buildings, floors and rooms, allocates beds and lockers to students and staff, and records visitors.
subs.problem: Knowing which room, bed and locker belongs to whom, and which rooms still have space, is hard to keep current on paper.
features: Define hostels, buildings, floors and rooms
Allocate bed, locker, table and bedsheet numbers
Place students and staff, filtered by class and gender
See rooms with beds still available
Log hostel visitors with ID card and photo
subs.benefit: Hostel staff could see who is placed where, which rooms have space, and who has visited, without searching registers.

subs.name: Library
subs.summary: Keeps the book catalogue with individual copy codes, prints barcodes, handles returns by code, and verifies the shelf by scanning.
subs.problem: Without copy-level codes and a shelf check, lost, damaged or overdue books are found late, if at all.
features: Catalogue books with copy-level item codes
Print barcode sheets for items and members
Return a book by entering its code
Scan shelf stock and note lost or damaged
Overdue, lost and pending-scan reports
subs.benefit: Librarians could find any copy, see what is overdue or not yet verified, and finish a stock check faster.

subs.name: Inward Outward
subs.summary: Keeps a register of letters and documents received and sent, with place, number, subject, file location and an attached image.
subs.problem: Paper letters and files are hard to find later when nobody recorded where they came from or where they were kept.
features: Record inward and outward entries with numbers
Attach an image of each document
Note the physical file location
Maintain lists of places and file locations
Filter registers by any column and export
subs.benefit: Office staff could trace any letter by number, subject or place and know where the physical file is kept.

subs.name: Utility
subs.summary: Year-end and administrative tools: roll data into the next year, promote or transfer students, and design your own forms and tables.
subs.problem: Year-end changeover and one-off setup jobs take staff time when each record has to be copied or changed by hand.
features: Copy master data and fee structures to next year
Promote students to their next standard
Move students to another institute of the client
Bulk year-end updates from Excel
Design custom forms and record tables
subs.benefit: Administrators could start a new academic year with less repeated entry and add their own simple forms and record tables.

subs.name: Document Templates
subs.summary: A template library and visual designer for certificates, ID cards, fee documents and admission letters, filled with school and student details.
subs.problem: Certificates, ID cards and receipts get retyped or reformatted for every student when the layout is not reusable.
features: Design layouts on a page canvas
Insert school and student merge fields
Preview with a real student's details
Keep drafts, publish, archive, restore earlier versions
Export as PDF or image
subs.benefit: Staff could reuse one approved layout for every student and keep older versions safe, instead of reformatting each document.

subs.name: Communication
subs.summary: Compose SMS, e-mail, app and WhatsApp messages to parents, and SMS to staff, by class or staff group, with message logs.
subs.problem: Reaching parents on several channels often means repeating work in different tools and losing track of who was contacted.
features: Pick a class and see each parent's contact
Contacts that cannot be reached are not selectable
Write e-mails with a subject and attachment
Draft message wording with an AI assistant, then review
Message logs with filters and CSV export
technology: Reports and exports of message logs
subs.benefit: Staff could reach the right families from one place, on any supported channel, and look back at past messages more easily.

subs.name: Circular
subs.summary: Publish school circulars to chosen classes or every standard, with type, message and attachment, and keep a searchable list.
subs.problem: Paper notices and scattered messages make it hard to reach the right classes and to find what was announced earlier.
features: Choose circular type, date, title and message
Attach a PDF or image to each circular
Target selected classes or all standards at once
Parents can be alerted in the school mobile app
Printable circular report for any date range
technology: Conventional circular register with printable report
subs.benefit: Staff could publish a notice to many classes together and find earlier circulars by date or class more easily.

subs.name: Parent Communication
subs.summary: Review messages parents send from the mobile app and the replies staff recorded, by date range, with student and class details.
subs.problem: Parent questions can get lost in calls and chats, so families wait without knowing whether the school replied.
features: Parents write to the school from the mobile app
List shows student, class, mobile, title and message
Each reply shows who replied and when
Filter messages by from and to date
Teachers see messages for their own classes
technology: Role-based access by class and subject
subs.benefit: Staff could find parent messages and their replies in one list, making follow-up on unanswered questions easier.

subs.name: Consent
subs.summary: Issue a consent for selected students of a class, then review issued consents with their parent status.
subs.problem: Collecting permissions on paper makes it hard to know which students were asked and where each consent stands.
features: Find students by section, standard and division
Set title, date and accountable status once
Issue the same consent to many students together
Consent report with parent status, filters and export
Select and delete issued consents
subs.benefit: Staff could raise a consent for a whole class together and later see which students it covers and its parent status.

subs.name: PTM
subs.summary: Define meeting slots for each class, let parents book through the mobile app, mark who attended and review bookings.
subs.problem: Parent-teacher meetings are hard to schedule and track, and it is easy to lose count of who attended.
features: Define time slots by class, title and date
Add several time ranges for one meeting day
Parents book a teacher slot in the app
Mark each student's attendance with remarks
Report of bookings with attendance and remarks
technology: Conventional slot booking and attendance records
subs.benefit: Staff could set up meeting slots once per class and see at a glance which bookings were kept and which were missed.

subs.name: Complaint
subs.summary: Record complaints with a date, description and attachment, then note the solution, who resolved it and its current status.
subs.problem: Complaints raised verbally or on paper are easily forgotten, with no clear record of who handled them or how.
features: Raise a complaint with title, date and description
Attach a supporting file to a complaint
New complaints start as pending automatically
Record the solution, its status and who resolved it
Complaint report for any date range, with export
subs.benefit: Staff could keep every complaint and its outcome in one searchable register instead of scattered notes.

subs.name: Mobile Apps
subs.summary: Manage the calendar, photo and video albums, exam schedules and leave requests that students and parents use in the school app.
subs.problem: Dates, photos and schedules shared through notice boards and chat groups reach families unevenly and are hard to find later.
features: Add class events and vacations to the calendar
Publish photo albums or video links by class
Upload exam schedule files for chosen classes
Review student leave requests, replies and status
Teachers can approve or reject leave in their app
technology: Conventional publishing to the school mobile app
Secure one-time sign-in from app to web
subs.benefit: Staff could keep school dates, photos and schedules current in one place so families find them in the app.

subs.name: Alumni Management
subs.summary: Keep a record of former students and run mentorship, job listings, events, surveys, donations and communication in one module.
subs.problem: Once students leave, schools lose touch, and alumni details, offers to help and event records end up in scattered spreadsheets.
features: Alumni records with career, education and achievements
Directory respects the privacy level each alumnus sets
Mentor matching, job listings, events and surveys
Campaigns respect each alumnus's contact consent
Donation tracking with receipts after verification
technology: Rules and automation for notices and reminders
Reports and exports with privacy masking
subs.benefit: Staff could stay in touch with former students, involve them with the school and keep their records current with less effort.

lines: Your whole school office, in one place.
From first enquiry to confirmed admission, then fees, attendance, exams, transport, library and every message home.
One set of records for every desk, so staff could stop re-entering the same details.

problem.label: A typical morning. Illustrative.
beats: Picture 9 a.m. at your front desk. A parent asks about last month's fee receipt.
The answer sits in one register. The student's file is in another, the bus list in a spreadsheet.
Three books, three versions of the truth, and the parent is still waiting.
By evening the same details have been typed again, in three places.
problem.turn: Scholar Core gives every desk one record to open.

intelligence.lead: Scholar Core reads your own school records and asks the questions your office would ask, then shows the records behind each answer.

family.summary: Scholar Learn brings courses, exams, discussion, curriculum planning and an adaptive learning engine into one K-12 learning module.
family.problem: Teaching content, assessments, lesson plans and student progress sit in separate places, so teachers rebuild the picture by hand each term.
family.benefit: Preparing lessons, setting and marking work, and seeing where students need help could become easier, with staff reviewing AI drafts.
technology: Knowledge graph of concepts and prerequisites
family.research: Question drafting designed from Bloom; concept notes use Webb DOK; framework views use CASEL, NGSS, NCDG; lessons use NCF and NCERT outcomes.
ai: Generates questions by Bloom level, showing options and the correct answer
Suggests concept tags and prerequisite links as drafts, never as facts
Writes short report summaries from recorded figures only
Rules decide each learning step; AI only phrases it
Drafts text in forms such as homework and exam instructions

subs.name: Teach/Learn
subs.summary: The course catalogue for each class and subject, opening into curriculum, chapters, lesson plans, a question bank and a concept map.
subs.problem: Teaching material, question banks and lesson plans are scattered across files, so staff struggle to find what exists for each chapter.
features: Browse courses by class and category
Open curriculum, chapters, lesson plans and question bank
Upload content or draft presentations for teachers
Generate questions by Bloom level
Review suggested prerequisite links between concepts
subs.research: Question drafting designed from Bloom's levels; concept notes carry Webb DOK levels; lesson drafts use NCF and NCERT learning outcomes.
technology: Knowledge graph of concepts and prerequisites
subs.benefit: Finding, preparing and reviewing chapter material could become easier, with drafts ready for staff to check and approve.

subs.name: Exam & Assessment
subs.summary: Set, collect and mark homework, assignments, worksheets, projects and exams, with question papers, blueprints, scanned answer sheets and a results dashboard.
subs.problem: Homework, papers and marking sit in separate files and registers, so teachers lose time chasing submissions and compiling results.
features: Assign work to chosen students or a whole class
Build papers from a Bloom and DOK question mix
Scan answer sheets; teachers approve marks before publishing
Mark assignments question by question with remarks
Students take a chapter diagnostic and adaptive practice
subs.research: Blueprints designed from published CBSE and Delhi Directorate of Education paper designs; question picking filters by Bloom and DOK tags.
subs.benefit: Setting work, collecting submissions and publishing marks could become easier to run from one place for teachers and coordinators.

subs.name: Engagement
subs.summary: A space where students and teachers raise doubts, discuss lessons and reply in threads, linked to subjects and chapters.
subs.problem: Students' doubts get lost between classes, and teachers have no single place to see and answer them by subject and chapter.
features: Raise doubts and discussions by subject and chapter
Reply in threads with teachers and classmates
Share with everyone or your class only
Search the feed by subject or see only yours
subs.benefit: Following up on student doubts could become easier, with each discussion kept against its subject, chapter and topic.

subs.name: Curriculum Planning
subs.summary: Turns the curriculum into month and period plans, tracks what was delivered and assessed, and shows framework signals for each concept.
subs.problem: Curriculum, monthly schedules and daily lessons are kept in separate files, so teachers and coordinators cannot see what has been covered.
features: See curriculum by subject and month, with NCF goals
Compare expected, delivered and assessed learning outcomes
Add, edit and review period lessons on a calendar
Track lesson-planning completion by subject
Browse CASEL, NGSS and NCDG signals per concept
subs.research: Lesson drafts designed from NCF and NCERT learning outcomes; framework views read CASEL, NGSS and NCDG vocabularies.
subs.benefit: Seeing what has been taught against the curriculum, month by month, could become easier for teachers and coordinators.

subs.name: PAL: Content model
subs.summary: Organises each chapter's content into four types, with authoring, review and a written rule set for choosing teaching methods.
subs.problem: Teaching content is hard to tag, check and reuse when each chapter's concepts, practice and fixes live in different places.
features: See chapter coverage across four content types
Edit content, add languages, restore earlier versions
Review AI-suggested tags before they go live
Keep a library of common mistakes with fixes
Browse learning units and teaching-method rules
subs.research: Content levels designed from Bloom's taxonomy and Webb DOK; framework tags use CASEL, NGSS and NCDG vocabularies.
subs.benefit: Preparing, tagging and reviewing chapter content could become easier, and the teaching rules could be read by anyone.

subs.name: PAL: Knowledge graph
subs.summary: Shows how concepts connect through prerequisites, from curriculum units down to single concepts, and where a class stands on them.
subs.problem: It is hard to see which earlier concept is holding a class back when prerequisites are not written down anywhere.
features: See which concepts must be learned first
Browse curriculum from units down to concepts
Open one concept to see its prerequisite links
Show AI-suggested links, clearly marked as drafts
Teachers see a class learning map and mistakes board
technology: Knowledge graph of concepts and prerequisites
subs.benefit: Finding the earlier concept behind a learning gap could become easier for teachers and academic coordinators.

subs.name: PAL: Learning engines
subs.summary: Rules choose each student's next learning step, with gamification, attainment reports, settings and AI controls around them.
subs.problem: Every student walks the same path through a chapter, so time is spent on what is already known and gaps go unnoticed.
features: Skip known concepts, repair gaps, recheck after days
Personal bests, streaks, badges and team challenges
Opt-in weekly challenge board, switchable off by teachers
Compare curriculum covered with what students demonstrated
Set AI policies, prompts and guardrails for review
subs.research: Adaptive rules designed from the Adaptive Learning Engine Developer Brief and decision records ADR-001 and ADR-002 on mastery and rule order.
subs.benefit: Students could spend more time on what they actually need, and teachers could see coverage next to demonstrated learning.

problem.label: An illustration, not your school

Last term's question bank is in one file, the exam blueprint in another, the lesson plan in a notebook.
Marking is on paper, so you chase submissions and compile results by hand.
Then someone asks who is falling behind, and you start the picture again from scratch.

family.summary: Scholar CCB helps schools manage staff capability: roles and competencies, tasks, talent records, HR operations and learning.
family.problem: Staff roles, skills, tasks, reviews and training sit in separate tools, so schools struggle to see who is ready for what.
family.benefit: Role needs, capability ratings, tasks, reviews and learning could become easier to connect, so development conversations could start from clearer information.
family.research: Capability Explorer designed from O*NET and SkillsFuture Singapore occupational reference data, per its source notes.

subs.name: Organization Management
subs.summary: One place for the school's organization profile, departments, staff directory, compliance duties, disciplinary records and role-wise screen access.
subs.problem: Staff details, compliance deadlines and discipline records are often kept apart, so ownership is hard to see.
features: Department pages with employees, job roles and SOPs
Staff directory with filters, status switch and CSV export
Compliance register with calendar, overdue list and templates
Disciplinary records by department and employee
Role and permissions matrix for screen access
subs.benefit: Staff, compliance and discipline records could become easier to find, and responsibilities easier to follow, in one place.

subs.name: Task Management
subs.summary: Staff tasks, projects, dependencies and deadlines in one workspace, with reports on delays and productivity and a full audit trail.
subs.problem: When tasks live in chats and spreadsheets, owners, deadlines and delays are hard to follow.
features: My Tasks in list or board view
Link each task to the capability it builds
Dependency map, timeline and milestone views
Deadline extension requests with approve or reject
Productivity and delay reports with audit log export
subs.benefit: Task ownership, deadlines and blockers could become easier to see, and staff work could connect more clearly to capability.

subs.name: Talent Management
subs.summary: Hiring, onboarding, reviews, internal moves, exits, certifications and capability ratings for school staff, connected in one lifecycle view.
subs.problem: Hiring, reviews, certifications and staff skills are tracked separately, so leaders lack a joined-up view of their people.
features: Hiring flow from job opening to offer
Onboarding journey with probation and confirmation
Goals, reviews and appraisals in review cycles
Rate staff on capability items from one to five
Development plans show gaps against role needs
subs.benefit: Staff journeys from hiring to development could become easier to follow, with capability ratings and role needs visible side by side.

subs.name: HRIT Management
subs.summary: Attendance, leave and payroll records for school staff, with approvals, configuration and reports in one HR operations area.
subs.problem: Attendance registers, leave requests and payroll papers are handled separately, which can slow approvals and month-end checks.
features: Punch in and out with attendance KPIs
Leave requests with single and bulk approval
Leave types, holidays and approval workflow settings
Payroll types, salary structures and deductions
Form 16, salary certificates and monthly payroll report
subs.benefit: Attendance, leave and payroll steps could become easier to complete and review, with records ready when approvals or reports are needed.

subs.name: Capability Intelligence
subs.summary: Capability and competency libraries, role-to-competency framework, command dashboard, skills graph explorer and mentor skill matching.
subs.problem: Without one shared skill language, roles, skills and required levels are described differently across teams, so gaps are hard to compare.
features: Library of job roles, tasks, knowledge, ability and behaviour
Competency library with clone, archive and CSV export
Map competencies to job roles with required levels
Dashboard filtered by department, job role and location
Explore skills and job roles as a graph
subs.research: Explorer designed from a reference occupational ontology sourced from O*NET and SkillsFuture Singapore, per its source notes.
subs.benefit: Roles, skills and required levels could become easier to describe in one shared language, so capability gaps could be easier to compare.

subs.name: LMS
subs.summary: Staff learning hub: course catalog, my learning player, course builder, session calendar, certificates and administration for training teams.
subs.problem: Training courses, sessions and certificates are scattered, so it is hard to see who learned what and who is due.
features: Course catalog; assign courses to people, departments or roles
Course builder with modules, lessons and quizzes
Map each course to the capabilities it builds
My Learning player with notes, discussions and certificates
Training sessions calendar with registration
subs.benefit: Training, sessions and certificates could become easier to organise, and staff learning could link more clearly to the capabilities schools need.

family.summary: Brings findings from several school functions into one view and helps spot where attention is needed, with the evidence shown.
family.problem: Leaders get answers from separate reports and personal memory, so it is hard to see where attention is needed, or why.
family.benefit: Principals and trustees could find it easier to see where attention is needed, understand why, and keep a clear record of what was decided.
ai: Findings come from fixed rules over school records, not generated text
Likely causes are written by people and shown only where approved
Explanations must cite verified evidence or fail the check
Recommendations are drafts; a named person approves, rejects or defers
Recommendation confidence is computed from evidence, never typed in

subs.name: Overview
subs.summary: A leadership overview of the school: health across key areas, what changed, where attention is needed, and the actions to take first.
subs.problem: Leaders piece together attendance, fees, results and staff records by hand, so it is hard to see where attention is needed.
features: Health score across school areas, with its working shown
Says plainly when data is too thin to score
Compares each class's attendance with the school baseline
Compares attendance with results where enough classes match
Priority actions, each with an owner and reasons
subs.benefit: Principals and trustees could find it easier to see how the school is doing and where to look first.

subs.name: Foundation
subs.summary: The base the insights stand on: departments, staff, students and capabilities, read from existing school records.
subs.problem: Insight is only as good as the records beneath it, and gaps in staff or department records stay hidden.
features: Shows each department's head and staff count
Flags staff records missing email, mobile or department
Student roll shown beside the findings raised about it
Define capabilities and assign them to people or departments
Brings school records in; re-running never duplicates them
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to see who leads each department and which records need completing first.

subs.name: Intelligence Loop
subs.summary: Checks school records against fixed rules, keeps the evidence for each finding, and walks it through review, decision and follow-up.
subs.problem: Issues surface in separate reports, with no shared record of why something was flagged, who decided and whether it worked.
features: Each finding opens to its evidence and reasoning steps
Likely cause shown only where a person approved one
Recommendations wait for a person's decision before any action
Marks an action verified only with proof and measurements
Shows checks that found nothing, as well as findings
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to see why something was flagged, who decided, and whether it was followed up.

subs.name: Analytics
subs.summary: Shows how findings, decisions and outcomes are building up: headline counts, decisions by status, and patterns the school keeps meeting.
subs.problem: Without a record of decisions and outcomes, leaders cannot easily tell which actions were taken and what followed.
features: Headline counts for findings, decisions and actions
Decisions counted by status, beside recorded outcomes
Recurring patterns noted, with how often each has recurred
Charts of staff, attendance, results and fee collection
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to review how decisions turned out and which patterns keep returning, without gathering figures by hand.

subs.name: Knowledge
subs.summary: Explore how the school connects, from departments to staff, classes and students, alongside a library of patterns and standard operations.
subs.problem: Who connects to whom, and what the school has already noted from past findings, is hard to see in separate lists.
features: Walk department to staff and class to students
Open findings appear on the item being explored
Counts knowledge, ability, skill, behaviour and attitude per capability
Searchable library of patterns noted from past findings
Library of standard operations with their trust level
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to see how departments, staff and classes connect and to revisit past findings.

subs.name: Automation
subs.summary: Where approved actions are queued and tracked, under a policy that a named person must decide before anything is done.
subs.problem: Suggested actions can drift or happen without a clear record of who agreed to them and what rules applied.
features: Approve or reject recommendations, with a reason recorded
Policy requires a named person's decision before action
Queue of approved actions with status and dates
Report the outcome so the record is complete
Task list shows the evidence each capability task needs
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to keep a clear record of who approved each action, and what happened afterwards.

subs.name: Account and Settings
subs.summary: Shows your role and what it allows, the school's settings, and an audit trail of what has been done.
subs.problem: When something is decided or changed, leaders need to know who did it and whether they were allowed to.
features: Shows your role and the permissions it carries
Audit log of actions, who did them, and when
Settings can be changed only with the right permission
Access follows each person's school role
subs.benefit: Leaders could find it easier to check who can do what in Insight, and to review what has been done.

subs.summary: Four short pages explain career certainty, ambition, alignment and originality, and let the student record the job they expect at age 30.

Student names the job expected at age 30
Student marks how sure they are
Optional entry for the job the family expects
Pick from the occupation list or type your own
